newsitem.title: USA: Atmel sees weak Q2 results.
newsitem.headline: Atmel sees weak Q2 results.

text.p: Atmel Corp warned Wednesday that results for its second quarter would be below expectations.
The company said in a statement it expects revenues for the quarter, ending June 30, to be about 10 percent below the $252.9 million it reported in the first quarter.
Profits are expected to be about 30 percent below the $38.7 million, or $0.38 a share, it posted in its first quarter, Atmel said.
Analysts had expected the company to earn $0.38 a share in the second quarter, according to First Call. In the comparable year-ago quarter Atmel had profits of $50.3 million, or $0.50 a share.
Atmel attributed the weaker than expected results to pricing pressures in its non-volatile memory business due to increased competition principally in the EPROM and Flash markets.

The company said that while it has started to book orders for its new products, many of those orders were not for delivery during the quarter and therefore did not help offset pricing weakness in the non-volatile memory business. The company said bookings in the second quarter should exceed first quarter levels.
